subject: Request: Custom SLA exhibit & order form language for Skyline MSA/SOW
messages:
From: Julia Martin <julia.martin@skylinehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Health Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>, legal@skylinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: custom SLA exhibit / order form for Skyline MSA

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for yesterday's call. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the standard Redwood MSA/SOW and we'd like to request a custom SLA exhibit and a few order-form language tweaks before we run this through our final signoff. High-level asks below so you can scope: 

- Availability: we need an explicit 99.99% regional uptime commitment for production endpoints in us-west-2, with an availability credit schedule tied to monthly uptime.
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency target of <= 200ms for our production model config (seq len typical 1024). Would accept a staged target during a 30-day canary.
- Exception path: request an availability-exception clause for planned maintenance windows exceeding 60s per week if pre-notified + mitigation plan.
- Evidence & audit: 12 months of request-level audit logs and monthly uptime/latency reports; SOC2 evidence references on request.
- Order form: explicit fallback routing allowance (e.g., to a quantized lower-cost variant) and a mechanism for temporary capacity uplift (burst).

Attached is our SOW draft (Skyline-SOW-Draft.pdf). Can you confirm feasibility and a timeline for redlines? We need a redline draft and a proposed DocuSign flow within two weeks to stay on our Q4 board review.

Appreciate it —

Julia Martin
Director, Procurement | Skyline Health
procurement@skylinehealth.com

--
Attachment: Skyline-SOW-Draft.pdf (application/pdf, 1 page - stub)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Julia Martin <julia.martin@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: custom SLA exhibit / order form for Skyline MSA

Julia —

Thanks for the clear summary and for the SOW. We're happy to collaborate on a custom SLA exhibit. Quick confirmation on scope and next steps:

1) Feasibility check: initial read suggests the availability and latency targets are reasonable, but we'll need Platform/OPS signoff on the 95p <=200ms definitive commitment for your traffic profile.
2) Canary plan: we can propose a 30-day canary with gradual traffic ramp and an interim SLA (95p <=300ms) that transitions to the 200ms target after successful validation.
3) Exceptions: we can include a planned maintenance carve-out and an explicit notification window. For unplanned capacity constraints we typically include fallback to a compatible model variant; we'll draft language that preserves throughput while protecting your SLAs.
4) Evidence: we'll provide one year of audit logs and monthly reports. If you need raw traces for specific incidents, we'll outline a secure transfer process.

Action items: I'll draft an initial redline for the SLA exhibit and order form language and circulate to you by EOD Thursday (11/11). Grace and Rishi — could you validate the latency commitment and list required telemetry/evidence items so I can include them in the draft? Ben — can you confirm any commercial/credits language we should propose for availability credits?

Attaching a working doc for our draft language: Redwood-SLA-proposal-v1.docx (stub).

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Success — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

--
Attachment: Redwood-SLA-proposal-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document - stub)

Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 10:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: custom SLA exhibit / order form for Skyline MSA

Hi all —

Quick technical note from Platform/Ops on the draft targets and evidence list:

- Availability: 99.99% regional is feasible for a production dedicated pool in us-west-2 with appropriate burst capacity and cross-region fallback. We'll outline notification SLAs (e.g., 72-hour planned-maintenance notice).
- Latency: committing to 95p <=200ms requires a few conditions: reserved capacity profile, pinned model variant (we recommend a quantized T4/aurora-optimized variant for production), and a traffic shaping policy for cold-start avoidance. We recommend the staged approach Logan suggested: 30-day canary at 95p <=300ms then go/no-go for final SLA.
- Evidence: ops will produce monthly latency/availability reports and rolling 12-month audit logs. For SOC2 artifacts we can provide a scoped summary; full SOC2 packages go through our security engagement process.
- Order-form language: we propose three items to include in the exhibit: (A) defined production region + fallback plan, (B) canary period & success criteria, (C) availability credit schedule by downtime buckets.

Attachments: ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx (stub) — includes metric definitions, required trace fields (request_id, model_variant, region, latency_ms p50/p95/p99), and evidence delivery cadence.

I'll add redline suggestions to Logan's doc and mark any items that require Sales/Commercial input.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Platform Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

--

Logan / Grace —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail. The proposed staged SLA with a 30-day canary and the interim 300ms target sounds acceptable to our engineering leads. A few follow-ups before we start legal redlines: 

- Please include explicit language in the exhibit for the fallback model behavior and the conditions that trigger temporary routing (e.g., capacity exceed, regional outage).
- We need a draft availability credit schedule (example buckets: <99.9%, <99.5%, <99.0%) and the mechanics for applying a credit to the monthly invoice.
- DocuSign flow: we prefer a single-execution workflow where Skyline countersigns the SLA exhibit as an annex to the MSA; please include the sequence and expected signer list in your redline.

If you can get the redline + the example credit schedule to us early next week (by 11/15) we'll circulate to Legal and finalize before their board packet.

Thanks — Julia

Julia Martin
